**Do you enjoy solving the data problems that are too hard to crack anywhere else?

**We collect and match pricing data from across the web, and it has to be complete, correct and fresh enough for our customers to act on. Some customer needs go beyond the standard setup: a new market to cover, tricky matching, data that's hard to get, or a customer-specific setup for a large enterprise deal. That's where you come in.

As Data Coordinator, you'll combine hands-on data engineering with ownership of complex data tasks and larger customer data projects, for both existing and prospective customers. And you'll help turn one-off solutions into processes and tools we can reuse across customers.

**About The Role

**You'll be part of our Product Success team and work closely with our Product Success Managers, GTM, our Solution Architect and colleagues across Product and Engineering.

You'll work on-site from our Aarhus HQ. English is our working language, and the team is international.

**Delivering data tasks and customer projects

**

• You'll maintain our data scrapers so collection stays accurate and tracking is uninterrupted.

• You'll translate requirements from Product Success and the Solution Architect into concrete technical work.

• You'll work on challenges around market coverage, data quality, matching, data availability and customer-specific setups.

• You'll own your tasks from technical investigation to quality-assured delivery, and keep stakeholders updated on progress, risks and changes.

**Investigating and solving

**

• You'll dig into data, processes and scraping issues to find the underlying cause and the right fix.

• You'll diagnose scraping bugs and turn them into actionable tasks for Engineering, and keep GTM informed when an incident affects customers.

• You'll extract, transform, validate and configure data with the right tools for the job.

• You'll document technical decisions, assumptions and completed solutions.

**Quality and scalability

**

• You'll validate accuracy, completeness, coverage and reliability before anything is delivered.

• You'll balance what a customer needs with what's technically feasible and maintainable in the long run.

• You'll spot recurring tasks and propose how to standardise, reuse or automate them.

**Owning the technical calls

**Within the priorities set by your manager, the technical decisions are yours: how to investigate and solve a task, which tools and methods to use, whether the requirements are clear enough to start, and which quality checks a delivery needs before it's done. When something needs input from Data, Product or Engineering, you pull in the right person.

You'll know you're succeeding when complex data deliveries land accurately and as agreed, risks are flagged early, and more of the recurring work becomes standardised or automated.

**What We're Looking For

**

• A background in data, e.g. from your education, projects or work, and you enjoy working hands-on with it.

• You know your way around Python, SQL or similar tools.

• An interest in web scraping and data extraction. Experience is a plus.

• You care about data quality and notice when something doesn't add up.

• You own a task from start to finish, and you clarify requirements before you start building.

• You communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders, including commercial teams.

• You enjoy working in English in an international team.

**What You Can Expect From Us

**

• Empowered collaboration: Work closely with GTM, Product and Engineering.

• Support and development: Regular coaching and feedback.

• Room to experiment: An environment where curiosity, testing and learning are expected.

• An international workplace: Colleagues from 24+ nationalities across disciplines and markets.

• Flexibility and balance: Flexible working hours, social activities, pension, health insurance and modern offices in Aarhus and Stockholm.

**About PriceShape

**PriceShape is a global leader in competitor monitoring and dynamic pricing. Our platform helps brands and online retailers track vendors' prices, stock availability, and trends while implementing tailored pricing strategies.

We’re a diverse team of 80 employees from 24 nationalities, working from a modern, centrally located office in Aarhus C. We prioritize work-life balance, trust, community and focus on personal and professional growth opportunities.

We offer flexible hours, social events, pension and health insurance, great work facilities and an in-house canteen.

**How To Apply

**If you think the position is attractive and suitable, please send us a job application and your CV as soon as possible. We process and interview on an ongoing basis. For clarifications about the position, you can contact Gregor Harms at **gh@priceshape.dk

Job Purpose We are seeking a highly experienced and hands-on Senior Optical Design Engineer to develop high-end optical products and technologies from customer requirements through optical design, prototyping, manufacturing, and final qualification.

This is a highly flexible and varied role where priorities evolve as projects develop. One day you may be designing and tolerancing a sophisticated optical system in Zemax; the next you may be developing Matlab or Python algorithms to diagnose a problem in a high-end CNC machining process, designing an optical measurement system, or working hands-on in the laboratory with production engineers. The ideal candidate is a strong optical designer as well as a curious, analytical, and pragmatic engineer who enjoys solving difficult problems across traditional engineering boundaries.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

• Optical & Lens Design: Perform optical system and lens design using Zemax, including tolerancing, sensitivity analysis, optimization, and design for manufacturability.

• System Integration: Translate customer requirements into practical optical solutions (imaging systems, non-imaging systems, precision opto-mechanical assemblies) with assembly, alignment, and measurement in mind.

• Advanced Optical Techniques: Design and apply strategies involving holography, interferometry, computer-generated holograms (CGHs), and compensation strategies.

• Lab & Production Diagnostics: Build and commission optical test systems, analyze measurement data, and conduct hands-on laboratory work to troubleshoot complex optical and manufacturing issues.

• Software Development: Write custom algorithms, models, and analysis tools using Matlab and/or Python to interface with optical design and measurement systems or support manufacturing processes.

• Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration: Work closely with mechanical, manufacturing, software, and process engineers, and participate in customer meetings to clarify specs and present designs.

Education & Experience

• MSc or PhD in Optical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical discipline with a strong emphasis on classical optics.

• Minimum 5 years of professional experience in optical design and development.

• Deep, practical knowledge of geometrical optics, aberrations, diffraction, imaging, and illumination.

• Demonstrated ability to build optical test setups, perform hands-on experimentation, and connect simulation results with real-world physical measurements.

• Strong mathematical and programming skills (Matlab/Python) to develop custom tools rather than rely solely on existing off-the-shelf software.

• Excellent communication skills, with comfort collaborating across fast-paced, fast-changing, and multicultural environments (including teams in Denmark and China).

• Advantage: Experience with CGHs, lithographic optics, holography, precision optical manufacturing, CNC/production process integration, photonic interconnects, photonic integrated circuits (PIC)

What We Offer

• High degree of responsibility and variety working on high-end precision optics.

• A role that bridges optical design, experimental optics, custom software development, metrology, and advanced manufacturing.

• Close collaboration with experienced international teams solving complex technical problems where conventional solutions fall short.

In addition to your CV, please include answers to the following two questions (should be included in your uploaded cover Letter):

1. Optical engineering challenge — 500–1,000 characters

Please describe one technically challenging optical engineering problem that you personally solved. Briefly explain:

• The problem and requirements – What were you trying to achieve, and what made the problem technically challenging?

• Your personal contribution – What did you personally do, including any optical design, simulation, programming, experimental work, or other engineering activities?

• The outcome – What was the result, and what did you achieve?

Please focus on a specific example from your own experience rather than describing a general project or team achievement.

2. Use of AI in engineering — 100–300 words

Please describe how you currently use artificial intelligence (AI) to solve or support development tasks in your present position. Give one or more concrete examples of how you use AI in your engineering work, and briefly explain what value it provides.

We are interested in your actual hands-on use of AI, rather than general views or opinions about the technology.

Spirii is looking for an Engineering Manager!

If you are passionate about cutting-edge software development technologies, leading agile teams, the EV industry, and creating outstanding products, join Spirii’s fantastic growth journey to lead the way for a sustainable future.

The Job

Spirii develops and provides world-class charging products and digital solutions to customers with electric cars. Our Digital Development department is proud to drive a listen, learn, and lead culture that allows us to constantly improve our ways of working. As Engineering Manager, you lead 1-2 of our engineering teams of 6–12 engineers and are accountable for making it a high-performing team. You own the people, the health of the team and the soundness of its engineering. You do this through others: Tech Leads and Senior Engineers guide the technical work day-to-day, and you make sure good decisions get made, quality stays high, and the team keeps getting better.

Spirii is adopting agentic development as the way we build software. AI agents are becoming part of how our engineers design, code, test, review and operate systems. You'll make it real in your team, working with colleagues across engineering to shape how we do it.

You work very closely with a Product Manager and a Designer. Product owns what we build and why; you own how well the team delivers it. You report to the Head of Engineering.

What You Will Do

Lead and grow your people

• 
Own the full people cycle for your team: hiring, onboarding, one-on-ones, feedback, career development, performance reviews and handling underperformance early and fairly.

• 
Build a team where people trust each other, take ownership and do their best work at a sustainable pace.

• 
Help your engineers grow, including senior engineers stepping into technical leadership.

Own team performance

• 
Be accountable for the team's delivery, predictability and quality, and for how it improves over time.

• 
Define with Product what good looks like, and track it with evidence such as delivery flow, reliability, and team health, not gut feeling.

• 
Turn priorities into clear commitments, make trade-offs visible, and protect the team so committed work gets finished.

Lead the shift to agentic development in your team

• 
Make agentic development part of how your team works every day, moving beyond individual experiments to shared practice.

• 
Adapt how work flows through your team as agents take on more of the building. That includes how work is specified, how code is reviewed and how quality is assured.

• 
Apply shared practices for quality, security and data handling as they develop, and stay accountable for what your team ships.

• 
Work with colleagues across engineering on how we adopt agentic development. Bring your team's needs and feedback, and help test and roll out new tools and practices.

• 
Track what agentic development changes for your team's delivery and quality, and share what you learn with other teams.

Ensure sound engineering

• 
Be accountable for the quality of your team's engineering decisions, including architecture, security, operational readiness, observability and technical debt, while your Tech Lead and engineers lead the design work.

• 
Make sure what the team ships is tested, observable and ready to run in production, and that incidents lead to real learning.

• 
Work with other Engineering Managers and Tech Leads to keep our platform and practices coherent across teams.

Collaborate across Spirii

• 
Partner with Product, Design, other departments and external consultants to align priorities and resolve dependencies.

• 
Communicate clearly and early about progress, risks and trade-offs.

Who You Are

• 
You care about people and want to build teams that grow, thrive and deliver.

• 
You hold a high bar for quality and for yourself, and you take ownership of results.

• 
You're genuinely excited about AI as the new way to build software. You want to be ahead of the curve, and you're curious about where it goes next.

• 
You're technical enough to challenge a design, read an incident and spot risk, even if you're not writing production code day to day.

• 
You communicate clearly with engineers, product people and leadership alike.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate has relevant experience with development of digital cloud-based solutions in an agile start-up environment and can take the responsibility for leading a team of developers.

We further look for a candidate with the following experience and personal traits:

• 
Relevant technical graduate degree at minimum bachelor level (engineer).

• 
3+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager with direct reports, including hiring, coaching and performance management.

• 
A background as a software engineer (backend or full-stack) building cloud-based solutions.

• 
Solid understanding of distributed systems, such as microservices and APIs, and what it takes to run them reliably in production.

• 
Experience improving engineering practices like automated testing, CI/CD, observability or incident management.

• 
Familiarity with DORA metrics or similar ways of measuring delivery.

• 
Experience making senior engineers and tech leads more effective, rather than doing their work for them.

It's an advantage if you have

• 
Experience leading a team's adoption of AI-assisted or agentic development, including changing practices, not just introducing tools.

• 
Experience with AWS and containerised workloads.

• 
Experience from eMobility products.

• 
Experience leading a team through organisational change.

Two innovation days per month for YOU to choose what you work on.

Senior ERP Systems Consultant – AX 2012 & D365 F&O

Mission

**Do you want to take ownership of two generations of ERP systems at the world’s leading maritime supplier of provisions and stores?**Do you have strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 and the ambition to play a key role in supporting our current platform while contributing to our transition to D365 F&O? Are you motivated by ensuring system stability and continuous improvement while helping shape the future of our ERP landscape?

If you are a technically strong ERP systems consultant who enjoys solving complex issues, collaborating across IT and the business, and building new capabilities for the future, this could be the opportunity for you.

Become part of our ERP team in Nørresundby, DenmarkReporting to our Team Lead, Thomas Jørsfeldt, you will become part of our ERP team, working closely with business consultants, developers, architects, integration specialists and stakeholders across our international organisation.

As a Senior ERP Systems Consultant, your initial focus will be our existing Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 platform, where you will ensure system stability, performance, technical quality and continuous improvement. As we transition from AX 2012 to D365 F&O, your role will evolve alongside our ERP landscape.

Senior ERP Systems Consultant with a focus on AX 2012 and D365 F&OYou will be our senior technical expert on AX 2012, acting as the escalation point for complex issues and safeguarding critical system knowledge. Working closely with developers, architects and business consultants, you will balance technical debt, maintenance and business-requested enhancements while ensuring that solutions meet our development, documentation and architectural standards.

You will also bring critical AX 2012 knowledge into our transition to D365 F&O, building hands-on experience with the new platform and gradually taking on systems responsibility for the new solution. This is not just an AX 2012 role – it is an opportunity to take ownership across two generations of our ERP landscape and become a key part of our future D365 F&O organisation.

More specifically, your key responsibilities will be to:

• Act as the senior systems and technical expert for our Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 environment, ensuring stability, performance, maintainability and architectural integrity.

• Troubleshoot complex technical issues and act as the escalation point for critical incidents.

• Work hands-on with AX 2012 development, X++, customisations, integrations, SQL Server and performance optimisation.

• Review technical solutions and ensure adherence to development, documentation and architectural standards, balancing technical debt, maintenance and business-requested enhancements.

• Protect and strengthen critical AX 2012 knowledge through documentation and knowledge sharing.

• Identify customisations, integrations, data dependencies and technical risks in the existing solution as input to the transition to D365 F&O.

• Contribute to solution assessment, data migration, testing, validation and cutover preparation in close collaboration with D365 F&O consultants, developers, architects and integration specialists.

• Build hands-on D365 F&O knowledge and progressively take on responsibility for the operation, maintenance, configuration, release readiness and continuous improvement of the new platform.

Profile

Qualifications & requirementsYou bring extensive hands-on knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012, supported by several years of experience from complex, business-critical ERP environments. You combine strong technical problem-solving skills with a structured approach to quality and documentation, and you are motivated by the opportunity to apply your AX 2012 expertise during the transition while developing your future role within D365 F&O.

Furthermore, we expect that you have:

• 3+ years of hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012, including System administration, development and architecture.

• Solid experience with X++ development and customization.

• Good understanding of SQL Server, databases, integrations and performance optimization.

• Experience from complex and business-critical ERP environments.

• Strong troubleshooting and analytical capabilities.

• The ability to balance operational stability, technical debt, transformation activities and business requirements.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills in English, with experience collaborating across functions and cultures.

• A structured and delivery-focused approach, with attention to quality, documentation and agreed deadlines.

It is an advantage if you have:

• Hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations.

• Experience from an AX 2012 to D365 F&O migration or another ERP transformation programme.

• Experience with Azure DevOps, Lifecycle Services, data entities, security, workflows or release management in D365 F&O.

• Knowledge of cloud ERP operations, automated testing or the Microsoft Power Platform.

• A relevant degree or Microsoft Dynamics certification.

Personality mattersYou are curious, analytical and collaborative, with a natural ability to take ownership and build trusted relationships across the business and IT. You enjoy solving complex problems, constructively challenging existing solutions and translating technical insight into sustainable improvements. You communicate clearly and thrive in an international environment where knowledge-sharing, teamwork and continuous improvement are key.

**We offer more than just a job

**We wish to be the best at what we do, and everything we do is based on our values of “Winning Attitude, Customer Orientation, and Getting it Done”. We offer flexible working hours and numerous employee benefits, counting a healthy canteen, take-away, free fruit, and fitness facilities. Wrist supports local elite sports, offering tickets to home games. You can expect free parking and access to Clever EV charging stations. Moreover, we have an active employee association that invites us all to play paddle, badminton, board games etc. and to join the yearly DHL relay race.

**Ready to apply?

**Please send us your application and CV via the “Apply” button. We want to fill the position as soon as possible and will continuously invite candidates for interviews, so do not hesitate to submit your application and CV.

If you have questions or want to know more about the team, please reach out to Team Lead, Thomas Jørsfeldt, at thjo@wrist.com or by phone on +45 2128 4416

**At Wrist, we are committed to cultivating a culture of belonging where every individual feels seen, valued, and respected

**As a global company, we aim to reflect the communities we are part of, believing that our strength comes from diverse perspectives, experiences, and the unique contributions each person offers. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, and we are dedicated to maintaining a recruitment process that is inclusive, fair, and respectful. By fostering a supportive workplace culture rooted in belonging, we lay the foundation for meaningful collaboration and shared success.

**Wrist is the world’s leading ship and offshore supplier of marine provisions and stores with a market share of approximately 12%. We are the only provisions and stores marine supplier with a global network of supply operations. We also offer services within owners’ goods and spare parts logistics, combining provisions and stores deliveries directly to the vessels. With the launch of the digital marketplace, Source2Sea, Wrist is leading the digital transformation of the marine supply industry. jobs.occupation: Chief Flight Instructor at GreyBird Pilot Academy - HQ located at Aarhus Airport, DK –  Ready to shape the future of pilot training? ✈️
jobs.description:
GreyBird Pilot Academy is more than a flight school. We are a fast-growing international business in an industry that never stands still – training the next generation of commercial pilots. Since starting out in Aarhus in 2013, we have grown to seven bases across Europe – from Dublin in the west to Helsinki in the east. Our students fly under the Spanish sun and across European airspace. Today, more than 200 students are training to become commercial pilots with us, supported by over 40 flight instructors and a fleet of 12 Tecnam aircraft, with 13 more on the way. This is where ambition becomes reality – where safety, people, technology, operations and training must all come together before the wheels leave the runway. You have an aviation background and have instructed from the cockpit yourself. With us, you will join a highly skilled team with short decision-making lines and plenty of room to shape our development. jobs.description:
Make business change land — across 30+ markets in a global customer engagement platform implementation that is 80% people and process, 20% technology.

Join us in creating a future legacy in medical dermatology. At LEO Pharma, we are global leaders in medical dermatology with 115 years of experience bringing innovation to healthcare. In Global Customer Engagement Platforms & Excellence, we partner across the business to enable customer engagement excellence — empowering global and local teams to execute with impact. We are guided by simplification, collaboration, and accountability.

In Global Customer Engagement Platforms & Excellence, we partner across the business to drive customer engagement excellence - empowering global and local teams to execute with impact. We are guided by simplification, collaboration, and accountability. Now, as we embark on a global Customer Engagement Platform implementation affecting around 1,500 users across 30+ markets, we are looking for a Senior Business Change & Execution Lead to make sure change lands across LEO - so the platform is adopted, used, and delivers lasting value.

Your role

As Senior Business Change & Execution Lead, you will run the business-side change and delivery engine that turns strategy into outcomes. Working closely with the Head of Global Customer Engagement Platforms & Excellence, our Business Process Owners, Global IT, and implementation partners, you will ensure that governance runs, decisions move forward, markets are ready, and change lands - wave by wave during rollout, and release by release after go-live. Business Process Owners decide how processes should work; you make sure those decisions move, land, and stick.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Owning the business readiness and adoption roadmap across markets and rollout waves, covering milestones, risks and dependencies, aligned with Global IT's project plan.

• Driving change execution: readiness diagnostics, stakeholder mapping, communication and enablement plans, adoption tracking, and go-live preparation.

• Running the governance cadence, including Core Team and delegate forums, and preparing SteerCo decision material, with clear agendas, decision logs and follow-up.

• Leading regular touchpoints with market Business Leads, and coordinating across Global IT, implementation partners, platform vendors, regional teams and local markets.

• Creating executive materials, stakeholder communications, briefing packs and change narratives that reflect LEO Pharma's business context.

• After go-live: running the roadmap prioritisation process with Business Process Owners, and tracking adoption and business value so the platform keeps delivering.

You will also help ensure that learnings are captured and acted on throughout the implementation, so the approach improves wave by wave. This is not a passive coordination role — you will bring structure, recommendations, momentum, and follow-through.

Your qualifications

We imagine that you bring strong experience from complex business change, adoption, transformation, or global implementation environments. You know how to make change work in practice - not only how to design the framework.

We are especially looking for:

• Proven experience leading business change and adoption in large-scale, multi-market implementations.

• Hands-on experience with structured change methods such as ADKAR or equivalent; Prosci certification is a plus.

• Strong execution skills, including roadmaps, RAID, governance, delivery cadence, and readiness tracking.

• Experience defining and tracking adoption and business value metrics, and using them to drive prioritisation.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills, including senior stakeholder and executive-level materials.

• Experience working with external implementation partners, platform vendors, and cross-functional global teams.

Experience from pharma, life sciences commercial operations, CRM platform implementation (such as Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud or Veeva), Agile delivery, or train-the-trainer models will be an advantage.

As a person, you are structured, persistent, and action-oriented. You simplify complexity, create momentum, and bring a clear point of view on what needs to happen next. You lead through influence rather than hierarchy - holding partners, process owners, and markets to their commitments while bringing people with you. You keep the end user in mind — because change that does not work for the field, the medical liaison, or the market team does not work at all.

What success looks like

• Markets are ready before each wave - go-lives happen without surprises, and Business Leads know what is coming and what is expected of them.

• Decisions move - governance forums produce clear decisions, owners act on them, and nothing sits unresolved in the log.

• Adoption is measured, not assumed - you can show where the platform is used, where it is not, and what is being done about it.

• Change is owned locally - Business Leads and market teams carry adoption in their markets, rather than relying on central push.

• After go-live, the roadmap reflects business value - priorities are transparent, agreed with Business Process Owners, and tied to measurable outcomes.

Your new team

You will join Global Customer Engagement Platforms & Excellence in Ballerup, Denmark. We are a global team working at the intersection of business process, customer engagement, commercial excellence, and platform governance. Together, we partner with markets, functions, Global IT, and external partners to ensure change lands, adoption sticks, and our platforms deliver real value.

A note from the hiring manager

I'm building a team that partners with the business and owns the outcome - not one that waits to be told what to do. Our global Customer Engagement Platform implementation is mobilising now - and this role will be central to making it land, from the first wave through to long-term value.

I believe in partnership as the work, real ownership within clear guardrails, and progress over perfection. You are not a coordinator chasing status updates - you set the rhythm, bring a point of view, and make it easy for others to deliver. If you can walk me through a time you made change stick across markets - and what you learned when it didn't – I would like to hear from you.

The opportunity comes with visibility to executive level.

Contact and application

For additional information, please contact Lisa Munkvold, Head of Global Customer Engagement Platforms & Excellence, at LIMUN@leo-pharma.com.

Beyond the skin

Join LEO Pharma, a global leader in medical dermatology, as we go beyond the skin to make a lasting impact.  Our innovative approach sets us apart. We are dedicated to leaving a legacy that positively impacts patients, colleagues, and our planet.

At LEO Pharma, we believe in the power of individuals to drive change. Our flat organizational structure empowers you to make a visible impact and offers versatile roles for professional growth. We value diversity and welcome applications from all qualified candidates, recognizing that our different perspectives, backgrounds, and attitudes enable us to make the best decisions. **The Impact You'll Make

Rather than focusing on only one stage, you can follow solutions from the initial customer requirement through design, implementation and commissioning.

You'll learn from experienced colleagues while building hands-on knowledge of frequency converters, drives, power conversion and electrification technologies, including applications within the marine industry.

**You will work on late-phase manufacturing science for new tablet products, preparing processes for large-scale market production.

**You Will Have The Opportunity To

**

• Drive scientific progress to reach project milestones, delivering on characterisation studies, test runs, and process validation activities.

• Work with production sites to solve technical challenges with blenders, granulators, tablet machines, in-process control systems, and process analytical technologies (PAT).

• Update and maintain critical process documentation, quality statements, scientific rationales and health authority submission files.

• Apply and uphold the relevant standards. Where a standard does not fully fit the situation, use your own scientific judgement to find the best way forward.

• Learn from how new ways of working meet reality at the sites, adapt your approach, and help update the standard so others can benefit.

Do you want to bridge the gap between a device and the customer using it? We are looking for an experienced Backend Software Engineer to help bring our IoT devices to life for construction customers: how they are configured, installed, verified and kept running. You join the Device Management team, work side by side with our firmware and hardware teams, and your work shows up in the telematics devices out in the field.

Bring our devices to life for customers. Your work covers the device lifecycle as well as building the internal tools our hardware and firmware teams use to debug them. It applies to new and existing devices, our own and third-party ones. You will build the backend that enables our devices' configuration, with AI as the core of how you develop.

**What's in it for you?

**

• See your impact. Your work shapes how devices reach the construction industry and how quickly customers can use them.

• Work close to the hardware. You design with the firmware team, whose building blocks you combine like Lego into new device configurations.

• Learn from experienced colleagues. You join a team with people who have 20+ years of experience and who are first movers on technology and AI.

• Work with AI every day. The team develops with Claude Code and Cursor, and you can contribute within your first weeks.

• Freedom and responsibility. The team has a lot of both, with an open door whenever you need input.

**Who are you ideally?

**You are a backend engineer who cares that what you build works for the people using it, finds the way to the goal yourself, and knows which people to ask along the way.

• Solid hands-on experience with Java, Spring Boot and GraphQL, including designing APIs and databases and the services around them.

• You are results-driven and self-driven: you unblock yourself, reach out to the right people early and follow your work through to delivery.

• You like to learn from the team and bring others along, and you can design a solution end to end, from database to service, and explain your choices to colleagues in firmware and across engineering.

• Domain knowledge can be learned. An IoT background, such as an understanding of protocols, is a plus, but we value learning speed more.

• Nice to have: Postgres (or another relational database), Kafka or other messaging, Cassandra, GitHub, and experience working with MCP tooling.

AI is the core of how our team builds software, including a shared AI development workflow. We expect you to use AI as your main development platform, or to be keen to. Hands-on experience with AI-first development is a big plus.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries, this is what we're looking for ideally. If you're excited about this role but your background doesn't align perfectly with every point above, we encourage you to apply.

**Primary Responsibilities

**

• Build new device configurations for our device administration tool, designed together with the firmware team, including bulk configuration updates for customers.

• Develop the backend behind them: API extensions, GraphQL, database design and orchestration, Java services and Kafka topics.

• Take features from the first idea to a device in the field, in close collaboration with our firmware and hardware teams.

• Support the rest of the device lifecycle, including installation, verification and the internal tool our hardware and firmware teams use to debug devices.

• Help the team grow: share what you know, review each other's work and raise the bar together.

****Our hiring process

****Don't waste your time on writing the best possible cover letter for the job. We want you to create an impact that matters, and that's not in the cover letter.

• Virtual meet and greet. Meet with the Talent Acquisition Partner.

• A deeper conversation: We'll go into your experience and how you work, and you'll get a clearer picture of the team, the challenges, and what the role actually looks like day to day.

• Assignment-specific interview. We want you to get an insight into some of the concrete work tasks or projects related to the role. You will be given a case to prepare prior to the interview, and at the interview, you will present the case to relevant colleagues from across Trackunit, who you’ll also work closely with in the job.

• If needed, throughout the process we will obtain references from former employers and do background checks for level specific, if you have not provided these yourself.

• Offer presentation and walk-through. We’re lucky to have you!

****Coming Together To Connect Construction

****We’re committed to construction - one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products – it’s a way of life at Trackunit. We’re proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

The question is: Are you in?

Curious about software, data, and emerging technologies? Join a cross-functional tech team, build solutions for real energy trading, and grow your skills alongside experienced engineers.

The job

Here’s what the job entails

In the role as Junior Software Engineer, you will help develop and maintain software solutions that support energy trading in the forward market in close collaboration with software engineers, traders, and business stakeholders. You will participate in code reviews, agile development activities and continuous improvement initiatives, while developing your technical skills and bringing fresh ideas to the team.

More specifically, your responsibilities include:

• 
helping build tools that solve real problems for traders and analysts

• 
working on feature development alongside experienced software engineers

• 
gaining hands-on experience with Azure, CI/CD, APIs, databases, and professional software development practices

• 
participating in agile ceremonies, code reviews, and team knowledge sharing

The team

Meet the team

We are a cross-functional product team supporting the Forward Trading business area across both software engineering and data engineering. Our primary focus is to build and operate software products that support day-to-day trading activities. We provide traders and analysts with access to market data, analytics and insights, and we enable trading capabilities and support emerging market opportunities. We also automate business processes to improve efficiency and reliability and deliver scalable and maintainable solutions in close collaboration with business stakeholders.

We are a team of nine tech specialists with various backgrounds and interests. Being cross-functional means that you will get exposure to both software engineering and data engineering, giving you the opportunity to explore different technologies and develop your skills across disciplines. We are a social team with a special love for funny memes and a competitive edge. We always seek to do our best and help each other out.

From day one, you’ll help build software used by traders and analysts making decisions in European energy markets. Your solutions won’t sit in a backlog or a sandbox. They will support real trading activities and new market opportunities.

Sara Helligsøe Hauge

Head of Forward Trading & New Markets Technology

Your qualifications

But enough about us… over to you!

As you will be working across both software and data engineering, we imagine that you are curious about technology and motivated to learn and develop your skills in a hands-on environment. You enjoy solving problems, exploring new technologies, and turning ideas into practical solutions. We also picture you as a team-oriented person who enjoys collaborating across disciplines while being comfortable taking responsibility for your own tasks. With a positive and proactive mindset, you are ready to contribute where needed in a dynamic environment.

Furthermore, we imagine that you:

• 
are studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related technical field

• 
have a keen interest in software development, AI, programming, data and emerging technologies such as agentic engineering

• 
have experience programming in Python and/or C#

• 
have some experience with SQL server, Databricks and streaming technologies like Pulsar or Kafka

• 
can work approx. 20 hours per week

Please note that prior knowledge of the energy sector is not required for this role.

We offer

We’ll take good care of you

At Danske Commodities, we take great care of our people. Joining us means you’ll get a lot of great perks – including social events, cultural experiences, tasty food and benefits to better your health, your life and your future.

Here are some of the benefits we offer our employees:

Shape your development tailored growth plans, 100+ DC University courses & Harvard Learning access

100+ yearly events from office parties to DC Sports events, CS:GO team, student network & more

Global career paths as part of our parent company, Equinor’s 20,000-strong international network

Flexible work lifeto fit with your studies

Unlimited paid child’s sick daysbecause family comes first

Free tickets & discountsculture, family fun, hotels, restaurants & more

Organic meals light breakfast, lunch, snacks, dinner & take-away

Barista caféhigh-quality coffee, always on us

On-site wellnessstate-of-the-art gym, physio, chiro and massage therapy

HQ in the heart of Aarhuswith stunning views, inspiring architecture and close to public transport

…. and much more

The process

Recruitment process and relocation

You can read more about our recruitment process here. Please note that if you are an international candidate, we will reimburse travel expenses in connection with potential interviews and support you with the relocation process.

About us

What we’re about

At Danske Commodities, we trade energy across 40+ markets and deliver solutions for energy producers and large-scale consumers.

Our people work together to find value in everything we do and deliver it. For our partners. And for the energy system as a whole. Together with our parent company Equinor, we operate on a scale few trading houses can match.

Our organisation is flat with an open-door policy. We expect you to care. About your work. About your colleagues. And about the difference we make.

Aspiring chefs, beekeepers, runners, parents, gamers – we’re proud of our diversity of ideas. What binds us together is that we all find average genuinely uncomfortable and want to do something about it.

We’re big on trust and providing the freedom for you to thrive. Together, we’ll make sure you’ll be the best version of you. Because happy employees perform better and we’re in this for the long run. No matter the stage in life you’re in, we’ve got you.

Join us. You'll love Mondays.

A workplace like no other

In 2025, we moved into our new headquarters in the heart of Aarhus – a workplace built for the precision, focus and collaboration that define how we work. With state-of-the-art facilities, our own barista café, a modern fitness centre and views worth coming in for.

Building AI keeps getting cheaper and faster. Deciding what's worth building, and getting an organisation to actually commit to it, does not.

At Heyra, we build AI systems, workflows and data platforms that are meant to live in production from day one. We work closely with companies that are moving quickly and need a partner who can hold both the strategic picture and the delivery reality in one head.

We're looking for a Deployment Strategist: the person the client's leadership talks to. You own the relationship and the outcome. You sit with a C-suite buyer, understand where their business is actually trying to go, and translate that into a sharp, sequenced plan for what we build and why. Then you steer a strong engineering team to make it real - without being the one in the codebase.

This is the strategic counterpart to our engineers. Where they go deep into the build, you hold the commercial and strategic frame: what problem are we really solving, what impact are we creating, in what order, and how do we get the organisation to adopt it. You're more product manager than a traditional consultant, with a strong strategic angle - closer to an Engagement Manager who's technical enough to make the right calls than a slide-deck advisor.

You'll work closely with engineers, data specialists, strategists and designers in a company where ideas move quickly and the distance from thinking to building is intentionally small.

What you'll work on

• Owning client relationships at the leadership level - being the person the C-suite trusts

• Framing the real problem behind the ask, and shaping it into an engagement worth running together with our FDEs

• Sequencing what gets built, in what order, and being accountable for the business value - not just the artifact

• Steering engineering teams toward outcomes, translating in both directions between the client and the builders

• Driving adoption: managing expectations, working with the people who have to live with the solution, and staying through the part after launch

• Scoping, structuring and de-risking engagements as they evolve

• Spotting where the next opportunity sits inside an account and growing it

**Requirements

****You probably have experience with

**

• Management consulting, change management, adoption, implementation of AI-native solutions.

• Owning client or stakeholder relationships end to end, with real accountability for outcomes

• Product, programme or engagement leadership in a technical environment

• Being technically literate - fluent enough in data and AI to make the right calls and earn trust with both buyers and builders, without needing to write the production code yourself

• Translating between business strategy and what's actually buildable

• Bringing structure to ambiguous, fast-moving situations

• The patience to sit with a worried manager, and the stubbornness to stay until adoption actually lands

Curiosity, taste and the way you think matter just as much to us as specific tools or years of experience. We hire for the who, not the what - experience is an indicator of perspective, not a deciding factor for how senior a role you'll play here. We're hiring across levels and shape the role around the person.

Why Heyra

At Heyra, we believe consulting needs to be rewritten. We're building a consultancy designed for the agentic era. We design, build, and operate AI products that change how enterprises work - from problem to prototype to production.

We care deeply about craft, speed and building things that work in the real world.

Heyra brings together people from engineering, strategy, product, startup and creative environments. We keep teams small, collaboration close and momentum high.

**You'll Join a Team Where

**

• people care deeply about what they build

• good ideas move quickly

• new technology gets explored early

• and where there is room to shape both the company and the way we work

We're around 50 people today after merging with Pyne, and we're only just getting started.

If owning how AI engagements get framed, sold and landed at Heyra sounds like your kind of work, send us a short note about yourself together with your CV. We care much more about curiosity, energy and the way you think than polished applications.

**Benefits

**

• Healthcare insurance

• Pension plan

• Parental leave

• Social gatherings

• New tech gear

• Central office

• Free lunch, coffee, snacks, and Friday beers

• Skill development

• Paid holiday

• Remote work allowed

• Pet friendly

Would you like to lead and further develop the Finance function at Denmark’s largest refinery? Kalundborg Refinery is seeking an experienced Head of Finance to combine hands-on operational finance leadership with strategic influence on site performance.

The high requirements for safety, operational reliability and regulatory compliance in a critical industrial environment require strong financial leadership, clear governance and the ability to create effective collaboration across site operations and Group functions.

Kalundborg Refinery is critical infrastructure within Denmark’s energy supply system and accounts for more than 15% of the country’s total energy consumption. Since January 2022, the refinery has been part of Klesch Group and operates alongside a sister site in Heide, Germany, and a recently acquired refinery in Gelsenkirchen, also in Germany. Under Klesch Group ownership, Kalundborg Refinery continues to operate with an uncompromising focus on safe and reliable operations, operational excellence and long-term value creation.

As Head of Finance, you will lead the full Finance function at Kalundborg Refinery and act as the primary financial steward and business partner to the Site Managing Director. You will be closely connected to Group and report to the Group CFO, ensuring alignment with Group finance standards, controls and reporting. As a member of the Leadership Team, you will contribute to the Company’s overall business strategy and take responsibility for both day-to-day operations and strategic initiatives across Finance.

You will have overall leadership and management responsibility for Controlling, Accounting, budgeting and Tax in Kalundborg. Your key responsibilities include:

• Ensuring effective and efficient management and execution of all finance-related matters.

• Ensuring operational excellence within Finance and compliance with applicable requirements and Company policies.

• Overseeing quarterly financial reporting and the preparation of annual financial statements, ensuring clean, credible and on-time reporting with no material control gaps.

• Overseeing and monitoring relevant direct and indirect tax matters.

• Preparing monthly management information for the shareholder and senior leadership team. Ensuring an effective and timely monthly financial close.

• Driving the budgeting process in Kalundborg with close coordination with project managers and Group.

• Supporting the management of structured finance arrangements, including preparation for and participation in bank calls, liquidity planning and liquidity monitoring.

• Leading and developing the Finance team, strengthening KPI dashboard reporting and building clear succession visibility.

The right candidate has:

• A degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field, combined with 8–12+ years of finance experience in multinational and manufacturing or industrial environments.

• A track record of leading a Finance team of comparable size, approximately 10–15 employees, at plant or site level.

• Strong command of IFRS and experience with financial reporting; consolidated reporting experience is an advantage.

• Experience with cost accounting, standard costing, capex appraisal, ERP systems — preferably SAP or equivalent — and advanced financial modelling and analysis.

• Fluency in a Scandinavian language and professional proficiency in English.

• The ability to operate confidently as a peer to plant operations leadership and manage stakeholders effectively across a dual reporting structure.

• Demonstrates dynamism and a continuous drive for results.

• Attention to detail and ability to present complex matters in a simple way.

• A demonstrated ability to develop and retain an engaged Finance team, communicate difficult financial truths with commercial tact and build strong functional capability.

The position is based in Kalundborg, Denmark. Travel (app. 2 days per month) is to be expected.
